submission.justification:
Radiator-R3 at 3 cm thickness is recommended as it provides the best pion/kaon separation performance while meeting all constraints. 

Key findings:
- R3 achieves 4.022σ separation at 3 cm thickness, significantly outperforming R2 (2.905σ at 3 cm)
- R1, despite having excellent separation (4.6σ at 3 cm), fails the transparency requirement and is therefore eliminated
- Among viable candidates (R2 and R3), R3 delivers 38% better separation performance
- The thickness optimization study shows R3 peaks at 3 cm (4.029σ), with performance degrading at both thinner and thicker values
- R3 passes the humidity ageing test with transparency loss well within the 10% limit
- The 3 cm thickness falls within the required 1-6 cm range

This recommendation maximizes the physics performance (pion/kaon separation) while ensuring long-term operational reliability through the 10-year mission lifetime.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the best possible pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c
requirements.evidence: R3 at 3 cm achieves 4.022σ separation (confirmed with 100,000 simulation events), which is the best among all viable candidates. R2's best performance is only 2.905σ at 3 cm. R1 is disqualified due to transparency failure.

requirements.requirement: Radiator must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: R3 is one of the three official candidates (R1, R2, R3) evaluated in the study.

requirements.requirement: Transparency loss after 10-year-equivalent humidity ageing test must not exceed 10%
requirements.evidence: R3 passes the transparency test requirement. Only 2 out of 3 candidates meet this hard requirement, and R3 is one of them (R1 fails).
The recommended thickness of 3 cm falls within the required range of 1-6 cm.
